newsitem.title: UK: British MPs back bill to target aid on poorest.
newsitem.headline: British MPs back bill to target aid on poorest.

text.p: A member of parliament who is angry that too much British overseas development aid is going to relatively prosperous countries won backing from fellow legislators on Wednesday for a move to help the poorest nations.

Opposition Labour Party member Hugh Bayley's application to parliament for permission to bring in a bill which would target the two billion pound ($3.3 billion) aid budget on sustainable development for poor people in poor countries was unopposed.

Bayley told fellow MPs that it was scandalous that countries such as India and Bangladesh were receiving less per head in aid than Hungary or Malaysia, whose per capita gross national products were more than ten times greater.
"A hungry man is an angry man, and an angry man is a dangerous man," he said.
Bayley's bill would outlaw aid projects which breach social, environmental and human rights norms, or which are linked to the sale of military equipment.
It has virtually no chance of being debated further in the current session of parliament because of lack of time.

But Bayley said he hoped that by putting down a marker now, he would encourage the new British government formed after an imminent general election to bring in more stringent rules to determine where aid went to.
